recon.notes: MULTI-EVENT PAGE. One WordPress page carries the entire 11-day official programme as plain text — 11 day headers with day-of-month only, the month and year stated once in the header block ("PROGRAMA oficial / BEARS SITGES WEEK 2026 / Del 3 al 13 de SEPTIEMBRE"). This is exactly the "festival-programme trap" the parser config warns about: an AI page classifier that sees "one overarching event" and reroutes to single-event extraction misses the schedule — the config keeps ai.classifyPages false so the heuristic multi-event path is used. The parser is automationEnabled: false, so it does NOT appear in scheduled runs (the 2026-09-09 run has no "Bears Sitges Week" parserResult); expect.extracted describes a manual run of this parser. Platform: WordPress 6.9.7 + Avada + WooCommerce, confirmed by a working /wp-json/wp/v2/pages/7256 endpoint; there is no events plugin — the "tribe-events" CSS hits are theme noise and the Tribe REST / ?ical=1 doors were not tried on instruction (known 404s). Text is Spanish with one English day (11) and bilingual fragments. Time tokens take many shapes: "19h.", "20 h:", "1h a 06h", "01:00h a 06:00", "21:30h to 03:30h", "20:30h. a 03:00h" — and on the 9th–13th the market's time sits in its own paragraph above the title. Half the 01h parties are written "1h" (no leading zero). Three ticket hrefs are typos of bearsevents.com (wwww., bearssevents, and one href that is literally the event sentence). The page contains three stale-year tokens ("INAUGURACIÓN ... 2025", "US: CITIZENS ... 2025", "Copyright 2025") and the linked map PDF prints 2027 festival dates.

coverage.basis: Static page (door 1) enumerated line by line under each of the 11 day headers; the rendered DOM (door 2) and the WP REST content (door 3) are text-identical to it, so all three doors agree on the same 79 h-time markers and the same activity lines — no delta. Published count = 48 dated, timed activities: 26 on the past days 03–09 and 22 on the upcoming days 10–13 (recon 2026-09-10). RECONCILING THE MARKER COUNT: 79 h-markers in the programme block; 78 of them sit on the 52 activity lines (most lines carry a start AND an end, the official dinner carries three, the excursion repeats its 11:30h, the Mr. Bear night has the 23h contest on a separate line); the remaining markers are on non-activity lines: 114:Mr Bear Sitges 2026: El concurso comienza a las 23h.. Every line with a time became exactly one entry EXCEPT: (a) "(Bear-Village abierto del 4 al 13)", the 23h contest line and the VIP-ticket parentheticals, which are traps; (b) no line lists two separate activities — the after-midnight parties (BEARS DISCO and BEARCAVE) are already on their own lines, so no splitting was needed. Untimed lines ("Osos en la Playa", "Descubre Sitges") are recommendations, not activities, and are recorded as traps, so no entry has startTime null. The daily repeats — Ruta del OSO (9 days), BEARS SITGES MARKET (7 days), pack pickup (4 days) — are listed by the site as separate dated lines with no repeat statement, so they are singles, as instructed; collapsing those three into series would give 31 entries instead of 48. Month/year for every entry come from the header block quoted above; every event line carries only the day-of-month. Flyers (doors 6–15) confirm dates/venues for 12 entries and supply the venue for the Meet Market party and the Drag Brunch and the address for the PopAir BBQs; two flyers disagree with the text on an end/start time (tea dance, drag brunch) — text kept, delta in the entry note. The linked PDF is the sponsor map and adds no activities.

openQuestions.q: After-midnight slots: the page lists "01h a 06h" parties under the header of the night they belong to (e.g. CAPITÁN Party under JUEVES-10), and the BeefMince flyers date them the same way ("THURSDAY 10 SEPTEMBER"). This file follows the header day, so startDate 2026-09-10 + startTime 01:00 is 23 hours BEFORE the real instant. Should the comparison tool (or the scraper) roll a start before ~06:00 to the next calendar day for programme pages, or keep the promoter convention?

The "1 9h: Meet & Greet" line has its time split across two <span>s ("1" + "9h:"); whether the scraper's text extraction joins them as "19h" or "1 9h" decides 19:00 vs 09:00 for this event. Untested here (parser is automationEnabled: false).

Flyer-vs-text time deltas: BEAR TEA-DANCE ends 20:30h in the text but 19.30 on the flyer; Sitges Drag Brunch starts 13h in the text but 12.00 on the flyer. Which should the calendar trust for this source?

The four BeefMince/Bearcave parties are marked belongsToSource "BEEFMINCE" (the club's own parser at beefmince.com/events). If that source documents the Sitges parties, add sameEventAs links here; the beefmince.json file was still not-started on 2026-09-10.
